adjudicated.jp: きゃつはそう言った。
adjudicated.en: the gal went and said.
adjudicated.assessment: きゃつ is a contemptuous or mock-archaic 'that knave/fellow.' 'The gal' identifies sex but loses the narrator's pointedly derisive register.

adjudicated.jp: リヤカーにして三台分ほどあった。
adjudicated.en: There were about three bike trailer loads,
comments: They load the stuff on the RV, so he's guesstimating I think. The question is why: the answer, they never take the RV. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: A リヤカー is a two-wheeled handcart. 'Bike trailer' specifies a bicycle-towed vehicle and changes the object used for the three-load estimate.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'There were about three handcart-loads in all.'

highlights.text: There were about three bike trailer loads,

adjudicated.jp: そこで桐原家の大きなキャンピングカーを使うことにした。
adjudicated.en: so we went and used the Kiriharas' huge RV.
comments: Why do the Kiriharas have a huge RV when the only way they'd use it is to get it on a train, as there's no way they can fit that thing on the only path out of town? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, role reversal, or independently actionable English defect.

adjudicated.jp: 走り屋マンガで学んだからだ。
adjudicated.en: because I've studied racing mangas.
adjudicated.assessment: 'Mangas' uses a nonstandard English plural for manga in this sentence.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'because I learned from racing manga.'

adjudicated.jp: ……見るとやるとでは大違いだった。
adjudicated.en: ...between the saying and the doing there is a vast difference in difficulty.
comments: "Easier said than done" + "Needlessly pretentious overliteralization for reasons of me being too awesome for words." -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, role reversal, or independently actionable English defect.

adjudicated.jp: いろいろあったが、とりあえず冬子はトラウマになった。
adjudicated.en: Several things have happened, the main of which is that Touko has become traumatized.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says only that various things happened and that, in any case, Tōko was traumatized. 'The main of which' invents a ranking and makes the trauma one event in a relative-clause list.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'A lot happened, but in any case Tōko was traumatized.'

highlights.text: Several things have happened, the main of which is that Touko has become traumatized.

adjudicated.jp: 二度と俺の車には乗らないとまで言った。
adjudicated.en: To the point where she said she would never ride a vehicle with me driving again.
adjudicated.assessment: 俺の車 is the narrator's car. 'A vehicle with me driving' generalizes her vow to every vehicle he might drive.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'She even said she would never ride in my car again.'

highlights.text: To the point where she said she would never ride a vehicle with me driving again.

adjudicated.jp: 同感である。

adjudicated.jp: いやー、シートベルトしていて本当に良かった。
adjudicated.en: Welll, it was a good thing we had seatbelts.
adjudicated.assessment: 'Welll' contains an unintended extra letter rather than a controlled marked-vowel spelling.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Well, it was a good thing we were wearing seat belts.'

highlights.text: Welll, it was a good thing we had seatbelts.

adjudicated.jp: とにかく『黒須家近所までは車を使えた』ので、あとはそこから移動すればよかった。
adjudicated.en: Anyway, we managed to walk away from the "Let's Use a Vehicle Up to the Neighborhood of the Kurosu Residence" plan, which was good.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says they were able to use the vehicle as far as the neighborhood of the Kurosu residence and only had to move the load from there. 'Walk away from the plan' says that they abandoned the plan and omits the successful transport stage.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that the car got them as far as the Kurosu neighborhood, leaving only the move from there.

highlights.text: Anyway, we managed to walk away from the "Let's Use a Vehicle Up to the Neighborhood of the Kurosu Residence" plan, which was good.

adjudicated.jp: とはいえ距離にして数百メートルはあってだな。
adjudicated.en: Nonetheless, there were still several hundred meters of distance.
comments: ...700? That's gonna be tough, since that's about the entirety of Kamisaka. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, role reversal, or independently actionable English defect.

adjudicated.jp: 俺と冬子はリヤカーを探した。
adjudicated.en: Me and Touko searched for a bike trailer.
comments: I.e. they don't have them now. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 'Me and Touko' uses the object pronoun as the subject of the sentence.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Tōko and I searched for a handcart.'

highlights.text: Me and Touko searched for a bike trailer.

adjudicated.jp: 冬子などはご令嬢であるためかリヤカーというものをフロントにカゴのついたママチャリだと勘違いしていたので、貧乏人代表として怒りの乳揉みをしてやった。
adjudicated.en: Perhaps because Touko is so much of an young milady from a rich family, when she mistakenly claimed that a granny bike was a 'trailer' because it had a basket on the front, as a representative of the poor people I massaged her breasts in anger.
comments: I think I read somewhere that even ojisans like granny bikes. That's very important information! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English begins with the ungrammatical article sequence 'an young,' calls the mamachari a 'granny bike,' and weakens the narrator's aggressive 胸揉み from groping or kneading her breasts to a neutral massage.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a grammatical sentence that identifies the basket-equipped mamachari and preserves the deliberately improper breast-groping action.

highlights.text: Perhaps because Touko is so much of an young milady from a rich family, when she mistakenly claimed that a granny bike was a 'trailer' because it had a basket on the front, as a representative of the poor people I massaged her breasts in anger.

adjudicated.jp: 殴られた。いいことだ。

adjudicated.jp: で、俺が探し出したリヤカーで三往復。
adjudicated.en: Then, with a trailer we found, I made three round trips.
comments: That's 6, plus the attempt with the RV. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says that the narrator found the handcart. 'We found' changes the finder to the pair.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Then I made three round trips with the handcart I found.'

highlights.text: Then, with a trailer we found, I made three round trips.

adjudicated.jp: 疲労困憊。
adjudicated.en: Fatigue at extreme levels.
comments: ...but he managed to make three round trips on a bike with a trailer in these hilly roads without dying. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 疲労困憊 is the complete state of being utterly exhausted. 'Fatigue at extreme levels' is an abstract degree fragment rather than an idiomatic account of the narrator's condition.

adjudicated.jp: 「……なに、この物置？」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "...what's even this storeroom?"

adjudicated.assessment: 'What's even this storeroom?' is not grammatical English question order and does not naturally convey the dismissive なに、この construction.
